- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next period; cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (0.00) and price is trending up, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect sentiment reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply a 1–3% upward bias for final 5–7 days.
- When model forecast is >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment.
